column1: # Known coverage gaps: one row per gap the archive can't close yet, read by `ea coverage`, the coverage pages, the polity hubs, and the twins.

# Columns: polity (us or a country code); state (US postal code, or a country's region code; blank for all); level (coverage level key, readiness key for grain candidates; blank for all); stage (general, primary, runoff, special; blank for all); years (YYYY, YYYY-YYYY, or YYYY- for open-ended); grain (results, county, precinct, fine, shapes, turnout, candidates, dates, party); label (what the row covers, shown on pages); ids (space-separated contest uuids; for candidates also government polity uuids, 14-digit Census government codes, or county FIPS codes; for results also county FIPS codes, which name a county's gap without matching any contest; blank for every match); category (known_gap: sources exhausted; blocked: a source exists but can't be reached yet; not_applicable: the grain doesn't exist); reason (one public sentence, through copydesk); sources (what was tried); checked (YYYY-MM-DD); ref (request id).

# A grain covers itself and finer ones (results, then county, then precinct). The most specific matching row wins: ids, then state, stage, level, the narrower years, and the earlier row. Rows that no longer match anything short drop off the pages; delete them when a source turns up.

column7: Community council elections in Scotland outside Highland
column10: Community councils are formed under each council's own scheme, not by statutory local elections, and cycles differ by council. Nearly all form without a ballot (Highland 2023 held 10 postal ballots against 116 formed unopposed). Highland's postal ballots of 2023 to 2026 and its notices of uncontested election still online are loaded (gb.cc_elections). Argyll and Bute (August 2026: 49 councils formed unopposed and the Cove and Kilcreggan poll), Clackmannanshire (2025: 6 formed unopposed and the Dollar poll; Sauchie and Tullibody have no notice), East Lothian (October 2025: 19 formed unopposed and Dunbar's result, which names those elected but gives no votes), Moray (October 2025: 13; January 2026: 2), Angus (December 2022: 2; September 2026: 19), and South Lanarkshire (October 2022: 34 formed unopposed; 2026 polls in Crawford and Elvanfoot, Biggar, and Rigside and Douglas Water with votes) are loaded. Orkney's 2022 declarations list only the people who accepted an invitation to serve, with their votes, so no complete count exists, and its scheme and the Evie and Rendall notice now return 404; Eilean Siar's only notice (Stornoway, 9 members) is an undated web page; Argyll and Bute's Lochgoil 2022 declaration is unread. Perth and Kinross (Pitlochry and Moulin 2025 and the Meigle and Ardler 2026 by-election; its other November 2025 notices are off the site), Stirling (2023, 22 of 42 councils), and Shetland (2025, all 18) are loaded. Dumfries and Galloway, Aberdeenshire, and Scottish Borders publish notices or names that are unread; Inverclyde and Aberdeen City's notices are unreachable even from a browser. Edinburgh, Midlothian, North Ayrshire, North Lanarkshire, West Dunbartonshire, West Lothian, East Ayrshire, Falkirk, East Dunbartonshire, Renfrewshire, Fife, Dundee, Glasgow, South Ayrshire, and East Renfrewshire publish no results on their sites; no national count exists.

Wikipedia's 1964 through 1996 Democratic convention articles carry no per-state table (only national totals) and web searches found no other free full text. An archive.org title search finds no 1968-1996 Democratic proceedings other than the 1988 lending copy; the Congressional Record (govinfo bound edition) search returns only whole-day granules with no reprinted roll call; and the free state newspaper archives that run past 1963 (California Digital Newspaper Collection, Illinois, Colorado, New York, and the Portal to Texas History) answer scripts with a bot check, so the San Bernardino Sun's AP tables went to a manual download. That download found the 1984 table (San Bernardino Sun, July 19, 1984, page 4) but only as OCR text too garbled to check against its printed totals, and its keyword search found no other year; the page images, and a page-by-page look through the other years' issues, are queued as a further manual download. Wikipedia's 1968-1996 Democratic convention articles still carry no table by state, and the California State University archive copies answer scripts with 403.

The Washington Evening Star's by-state tables for the 1932 first ballot, the 1940 sixth ballot, the 1948 first and second ballots, and the 1952 final count are loaded as defaults; its 1936, 1944, and 1960 issues from the day after the nomination print only the national count in prose (Landon 984 and Borah 19; Dewey 1,056 and MacArthur 1; Nixon 1,321 and Goldwater 10, ten Louisiana delegates), the first five 1940 ballots and the third 1948 ballot are not printed by state, and the Star's scan ends on December 31, 1963, so the 1964 convention is not in it. A full-text search of the Library of Congress's other digitized newspapers for the days after the 1936, 1944, 1956, and 1960 conventions found no other by-state table. A page-image capture of the two Internet Archive lending copies was attempted on 2026-11-13 and produced no images, so the 1952 first-called roll and the 1964 roll call remain unread. Rechecked 2026-11-13 against the full page text of every Evening Star page of 1936-06-11/12, 1940-06-27/28/29, 1944-06-28/29, and 1948-06-24/25/26: none holds a state-by-state tally (the only table is a blank tally sheet in the 1940-06-27 issue), so these ballots stay unread.

column7: Villages moved between provinces and ilçeler
column10: Provinces from 1926 to 1957 are unions of whole present-day ilçeler, so a village or nahiye that changed province without taking its ilçe's whole outline is not drawn: the nahiye-level seats assumed to follow their kaza (Adaklı, Yayladere, Yedisu, Karlıova, Erzin, Payas, Sumbas, Yumurtalık, Erdemli, Çamlıyayla, Derecik, Uludere, Doğanşar, Akıncılar, Çamoluk, Ağaçören, and Sarıyahşi), the villages Law 3711 gave Hassa from the annexed land, the villages of Law 6429's Nevşehir and Kırşehir central kazas, and the border villages between neighboring provinces such as Ağrı's, which differ slightly from today's. Transfers after 1957 are not drawn either: Law 714 (Resmî Gazete 12213, 1966-01-29) moved Kaynarca ilçe from Kocaeli to Sakarya, but the ilçe is not in tkgm_districts.tsv or tkgm_parents.tsv, and no outline vintage runs past 1957. Şaşmaz (2022) is unchecked, and the sources hold no record tying it to a province move. Checked 2026-11-02: Law 3711 leaves the Hassa villages from the annexed land to a later executive decision (article 3 and its note), Law 6429's schedule gives only village counts for each nahiye (Nevşehir Merkez 11, Acıgöl 13, Derinkuyu 8; Kırşehir Merkez 41, Çoğun 26) and no names, and no law text prints the nahiye moves; the 1940 census book lists Karlıova as a kaza and Yumurtalık, Payas, and Erzin among Seyhan or Hatay towns, so the nahiye seats stay with their kaza and no transfer row is added.

column7: Ten köy muhtarlıks missing from YSK's files
column10: YSK counts 18,152 köys in 2024, but its ballot-box results and muhtarlık list name only 18,142. TÜİK 2023 matches none of the 123 beyond the YSK pairing, since its list is held only as YSK-keyed rows. The 10 are probably among the 13 with an earlier register entry, but no source names them, so the row stays blocked. YSK's 31 Mart 2024 bulletin §3.1.2 (read from its Wayback copy, 60 pages) gives only the national counts, with no köy count per ilçe and no other köy figure anywhere in the document, so the per-ilçe test cannot be run from it. TÜİK's ADNKS tables on veriportali.tuik.gov.tr (DF_ADNKS_T22 and T15) publish population by il and ilçe with belde and köy combined, not per köy, and its data API answers 403; a search for an NVİ UAVT export or a Mahalli İdareler köy list by ilçe found none outside e-İçişleri and adres.nvi.gov.tr (both already failed). Closed as a known gap (class column in pipelines/ea/sources/tr/e_icisleri_2024_unmatched.tsv).

column7: Party primaries by county still missing: the 1918 Socialist primaries
column10: The 1919 Legislative Manual prints them by county (PDF pages 299-311, 323-354, and 371-380) as 200 ppi scans, but its text layer drops columns and rows, misreads the totals rows, and splits tables across pages, so each page needs its columns named from the image and its cells checked against the totals; the 1914 Republican, Democratic, and Socialist statewide and congressional primaries, the 1916 Republican, Democratic, and Socialist statewide and congressional primaries (the printed totals for Cuthbert and Simon each leave out one county), the 1918 Republican and Democratic statewide and congressional primaries, and the March 21, 1916 Republican, Democratic, and Socialist presidential preference primaries (president only; Estabrook's county column adds to 9,823 against a printed 9,851, and the Socialist scattering votes have no county breakdown) are loaded (us.nd_primaries); 1914 scattering votes are not loaded. The 1918 Socialist tables (pages 378-379) head each column with an office but no candidate name, and print counts of 0 to 13 per county, so no candidate can be credited.

column10: The National Election Commission's statistics system gives the presidential elections of 1952 through 1967 by city, county, and district only; its polling-district and neighborhood reports return no rows for those years.
column11: info.nec.go.kr electionInfo_report.xhtml VCCP08 (statements VCCP08_#91 and VCCP08_#1) and VCCP04, queried for Seoul's districts in each of the five elections

column7: Supplementary elections for governor of Amazonas (2017) and Tocantins (2018)
column10: Both states reran the governor election in two rounds (Amazonas 6 and 27 August 2017, Tocantins 3 and 24 June 2018). The electoral court's open-data files hold no supplementary rows for either, and its site and the regional courts answer scripts with Access Denied, so the results are queued for a manual download.
column11: TSE supplementary elections calendar (tse.jus.br/eleicoes/eleicoes-suplementares/calendarios/calendario-das-eleicoes-suplementares-2017)

column10: The Federal Statistical Office publishes cantonal votes by commune as open data only from the vote of 10 February 2019. Earlier results are in each canton's own archive (statistical offices, official gazettes, and state chancelleries), in 24 different formats; votes held at the Landsgemeinde in Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden are a separate class.
column11: Federal Statistical Office, Echtzeitdaten am Abstimmungstag zu kantonalen Abstimmungsvorlagen (opendata.swiss), first file sd-t-17-02-20190210-kantAbstimmung.json

column7: Dates of the Second Republic and Second Empire legislative elections, and of the Revolution-era, 1815, 1851, 1852, and 1870 plebiscites
column10: No official list online; Assemblée nationale history pages and Gallica Moniteur universel issues were not reached.
column11: Assemblée nationale, Sycomore history of the legislatures; Gallica Moniteur universel

column7: Dates of the censitary chamber elections of the Restoration and July Monarchy
column10: No official list online; no national series of results is known.
column11: Assemblée nationale, Sycomore; Gallica Journal des débats

column7: Parlamento de Galicia elections of 1981 to 1997
column10: The Xunta de Galicia's open-data catalog starts with the 2001 election, so the elections of 1981, 1985, 1989, 1993, and 1997 wait for the Xunta Electoral de Galicia's results acordos in the Diario Oficial de Galicia or another official file.
column11: datos.gob.es catalog of publisher A12002994 (Eleccións ao Parlamento de Galicia, resultados 2001-2024); abertos.xunta.gal

column7: Scottish regional and district divisions of 7 May 1974 with no candidate and no count: Caithness 7, Ross and Cromarty 7 and 15, Inverness 7 and 15, and Dundee 4
column10: The Bochel and Denver volume prints "No Candidate" for these five wards and marks Dundee 4 (Craigiebank) as no election due to the death of a candidate, with no votes; they are left out and each council election carries a note. The other 1,617 divisions and wards are loaded with their printed names where the volume gives them.
column11: Bochel and Denver, Scottish Regional and District Elections 1974 (Elections Centre scan)

column7: 2010 Acre time zone referendum below the state
column10: The Acre electoral court published the referendum only as a state total, and the national electoral court's 2010 section files hold the presidential and general ballots but not the referendum's second ballot box.
column11: TRE-AC Referendo 2010 totalization report (Wayback 2014-10-06); TRE-AC Plebiscitos e referendos page (Wayback 2012-02-10); TSE votacao_secao_2010_AC

column7: Perth and Kinross District ward 1 (Perth Central), 3 May 1977
column10: The volume prints 371 and 271 votes with a majority of 50, so one figure is misprinted and the ward is left out rather than guessed. No council record or press report of the result was found online; the Perthshire Advertiser and The Courier of May 1977 would settle it.
column11: Bochel and Denver, Scottish District Elections 1977 (Elections Centre scan), page 48

column7: Midlothian District Council election of 5 May 1988
column10: The scanned 1988 district volume skips its page 40 (the PDF runs from page 39, the end of Edinburgh, to page 41, East Lothian), which holds Midlothian, so none of its wards are loaded, while the other 52 district councils are. No council or press source for the ward results was found online.
column11: Bochel and Denver, Scottish District Elections 1988 (Elections Centre scan), pages 39 and 41

column7: President Evren, elected by the constitutional referendum
column10: Kenan Evren became President by the 7 November 1982 constitutional referendum (provisional article 1 of the 1982 Constitution), not by an Assembly vote, so no round of voting is counted for 1982 and the class has no date for it.
column11: TBMM Tutanak Dergisi; 1982 Constitution, provisional art. 1 (https://www.mevzuat.gov.tr/MevzuatMetin/1.5.2709.pdf)

column7: Election days of the Empire's Chamber of Deputies elections other than 1863, 1869, 1872, 1878, 1881, 1884, 1886, and 1889
column10: The Câmara's Cronologia do funcionamento (1826-1992) reproduces only the decrees that dissolved a chamber and named the next polling day, so the days for 1826-1860, 1867, and 1876 are stated by year only (Wikipedia template); the Collecção das Leis do Império decrees and the electoral instructions that set them are not yet read, and no province-level contests or seat counts are loaded.
column11: Câmara dos Deputados Cronologia do funcionamento da Câmara dos Deputados 1826-1992 (bd.camara.leg.br/bd/handle/bdcamara/31679); Senado Tabela de Legislaturas

column7: Mayors of cities, towns, villages, and Tokyo special wards (about 1,741 offices)
column10: No national body publishes mayoral results: the ministry compiles only the 20 designated-city mayors (PDF since 2011) and the unified-election summary counts, so candidate votes for the other municipalities sit in each municipal election commission's own pages, which have not been gathered yet.
column11: MIC pages 選挙関連資料 (soumu.go.jp/senkyo/senkyo_s/data/) and 政令市市長選挙結果

column7: Scottish council wards of 3 May 2012 with first preferences only, no STV stage counts: 326 of 353
column10: Stage counts are loaded for 27 wards (Aberdeenshire 18 of 19 and East Ayrshire 9) from the councils' own Election Results reports, whose fractional stage values sum exactly to the valid votes. Ellon and District is left out because the council's report prints Owen's stage 3 total as 761.61561 where his stage 2 total and the transfer give 764.61561, so stage 3 sums to 4208 of 4211 valid votes. The other councils' 2012 pages hold declarations of result with first preferences and the stage of election only (North Ayrshire, Dundee), summaries without transfers (Edinburgh), or are not yet searched; every ward without a count has only the first preferences and elected from the Local Elections Archive Project.
column11: Council election results pages; Internet Archive

column7: Scottish council wards of 3 May 2007 with first preferences only, no STV stage counts: 353 of 353
column10: The councils' 2007 count reports have not been searched for yet; the wards have only the first preferences and elected from the Local Elections Archive Project.
column11: Council election results pages; Internet Archive

column7: Comarca and entidad menor unit counts
column10: The Registro de Entidades Locales (REL) host returned empty responses through the Spanish VPN, so the dated counts of comarcas and entidades locales menores are not loaded.
column11: Ministerio de Política Territorial, Registro de Entidades Locales

column7: DPRD regency and city votes by electoral district
column10: KPU open data holds only 2019 seats per party per dapil (dataset 33); party and candidate votes sit in each regency or city commission decree and site, with no national file.
column11: opendata.kpu.go.id/ds/33; jdih.kpu.go.id

column10: No national body publishes candidate votes for prefectural assembly districts: the ministry's 地方選挙結果調 books (2003-2019) give only counts by prefecture for the April unified elections, so district results sit in each prefectural election commission's own pages, which have not been gathered yet.
column11: MIC 地方選挙結果調 (soumu.go.jp/senkyo/senkyo_s/data/chihou/ichiran.html), 2019 book section 4

column10: KPU open data holds only winners with votes and contest totals for 2006-2018 (ds/12-17); the pilkada results sites are offline or time out, and the per-candidate declarations sit with about 514 regency and city commissions, with no national file.
column11: opendata.kpu.go.id ds/12-17; pilkada2024.kpu.go.id (offline)

column7: Provincial legislature (DPRD provinsi) candidate and party votes by constituency
column10: KPU open data holds only 2019 seats per party per provincial constituency; votes sit in the result decrees of the 38 provincial KPUs, not gathered.
column11: opendata.kpu.go.id/ds/74

column7: Governor elections (pilkada) ticket votes by province
column10: KPU open data (ds/12-17) holds only winning tickets with their votes for 2006-2008, 2010, 2017, and 2018; all-ticket results for every wave sit in provincial KPU decrees, not gathered.
column11: opendata.kpu.go.id/ds/12 to ds/17
